title: The Top Xero Integrations for 2026 to Automate Xero Reconciliation and Eliminate Manual Entry
summary: Manual Xero entry eats days each month. The best Xero integrations and add-ons cut close to hours. Compare 9 apps for ecommerce and SaaS, ranked for 2026.
body_markdown:
The best Xero integrations remove your most expensive manual step, and each one has to earn its monthly fee. For ecommerce and SaaS teams, that step is usually payout reconciliation, followed by inventory, receipts, sales tax, and payroll. For example, if you still split Stripe or Shopify deposits into sales, fees, and refunds by hand, month-end takes days.


However, with[over 1,000 apps](https://www.xero.com/us/accounting-software/app-integrations/) for[4.92 million Xero customers](https://brandfolder.xero.com/NE531UQB/as/bx8xwhj65zjm36s5fn4kc4gx/Xero_FY26_Annual_Results_Investor_Presentation) , more integrations don’t automatically mean less work, so careful selection beats sheer volume. That’s why this guide ranks 9 Xero integrations by use case, with pricing, ratings, and pros and cons.


**With this guide, you can:**


- Compare 9 Xero integrations by sync method, multi-currency support, COGS, and starting price to find the best fit for your business.
- Choose the right integration stack for your business type and transaction volume, prioritizing tools that automate sales, payouts, fees, refunds, and taxes.
- Avoid six common reconciliation errors that prevent your Xero books from balancing, including duplicate syncs and incorrectly recorded payouts.
- Reduce manual work and improve accuracy by focusing on your biggest accounting bottleneck first and choosing integrations that can scale with your business.


## **What is an integration with Xero?**


A[Xero integration](https://synder.com/integrations/xero/) is a link that enables data to flow between two applications in real time, using Xero’s open API, without having to be re-entered into Xero. Apps that integrate with Xero cover every step between a sale and a closed month. A properly designed integration automatically splits these into the right general ledger accounts:


- Gross sales
- Processing fees
- Refunds
- Taxes


As a result, you don’t have to take a net sum and distribute it by hand.


**The main categories, with example apps:**


- **Payroll** : Gusto, the provider behind Xero Payroll in the US, posts wage and tax journals.
- **Sales and payouts:** Synder and the free Shopify integration by Xero post sales, fees, refunds, and payouts.
- **Payments** : Payment integrations such as Stripe let your customers settle Xero invoices by card, Apple Pay, or Google Pay.
- **Inventory** : Cin7 Core and Unleashed post COGS and stock values to Xero.
- **Document capture** : Hubdoc and Dext extract supplier bill and receipt data.
- **Sales tax** : Avalara AvaTax calculates the tax and files returns.


### **Xero add-on, plugin, or integration: what’s the difference?**


The difference between a Xero add-on and a Xero integration is who builds and supports it. Xero add-ons are built and supported by Xero, such as Hubdoc and Xero Projects, while third-party vendors build and maintain integrations that connect through Xero’s API.


“Xero plugins” is another name for the same third-party apps, which connect through Xero’s secure OAuth 2.0 login.


### **Is Xero API free?**


The Xero API is free for business owners, because the app vendor pays for access and you cover only the subscription. Since March 2, 2026, the[Xero Developer Platform](https://developer.xero.com/pricing) has billed vendors from the free Starter tier to Advanced at $895 a month, and[bans training AI models on API data](https://www.accountingtoday.com/news/xero-shifts-to-tiered-pricing-model-for-developers) .


## **How we evaluated these Xero integration partners**


We scored every app on this list, Synder included, against the same five criteria, because star ratings alone won’t tell you which app keeps your Xero books tying out:


1. Ledger accuracy: does it post gross sales, fees, refunds, and tax to separate accounts instead of one net figure?
2. Flexible sync modes: can you choose per-transaction posting for full detail or daily or monthly summaries for high volumes, and does each payout still match the bank deposit?
3. Scale: what are the per-plan transaction, order, or document limits, and what happens when you outgrow them?
4. Total cost: what is the published starting price, how does it grow with volume, and is there a free trial?
5. Xero App Store certification and reviews: is it listed there, and how does its G2 rating compare with its Capterra and Xero marketplace scores?


The best Xero integration for your business is the one that scores well on the criteria you care about most. Synder publishes this guide and appears on the list, so it was held to the same criteria, limitations included, as every other app. Prices come from vendors’ official pages.

### **1. Synder, best for multi-channel, multi-currency payout reconciliation**


Synder ratings:[Xero App Store](https://apps.xero.com/app/synder) 4.7 (147 reviews) ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/185441/Business-Payments/reviews/) 4.7 (256 reviews) ·[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/synder/reviews) 4.7 (249 reviews)


[Synder](https://synder.com/) is an accounting automation platform that links ecommerce data and payments from more than 30 different sources into Xero, such as:


- Stripe
- Shopify
- Amazon
- PayPal
- Square


It’s listed on the[Xero App Store](https://apps.xero.com/app/synder) and takes messy payment information and turns it into accurate accounting data.


With the[Auto-reconcile Xero transactions](https://synder.com/help/automatic-xero-bank-reconciliation-feature/) setting switched on, Synder also marks the income and expense entries it syncs to your clearing account as reconciled. Payouts are the exception: Xero doesn’t let third-party apps mark bank transfers as reconciled, so Synder syncs them as unreconciled, and you confirm them in Xero yourself.


**Key features**


- [Synder Sync](https://synder.com/industry/syndersync/) offers two modes: Per Transaction mode syncs each sale, refund, fee, and tax individually with customer and product detail. Summary Sync mode combines a day’s or a month’s activity into a single record, which Synder posts to Xero as an invoice with payments and a credit note with refunds.
- Synder separates fees, refunds, and taxes during sync and moves each payout to your bank through a clearing account.
- [Transaction Reconciliation](https://synder.com/blog/transaction-reconciliation/) matches clearing-account lines to the platform’s own records via API, standard upload, or custom mapping. For Stripe, Shopify, and Amazon, Synder pulls the records via API, so you don’t import a file. PayPal needs its predefined activity report, and other sources use a CSV or XLSX upload.
- With Xero, you also export the Account Transactions report once and upload it, because no API provides that file, and Synder then handles the matching. Anything that doesn’t tie 100% is flagged, so you review only what needs attention.
- [Balance Reconciliation](https://synder.com/blog/balance-reconciliation/) verifies synced data against the platform’s starting and ending balances for a chosen period.
- [Synder RevRec](https://synder.com/industry/revenue-recognition/) , an additional module, posts GAAP and ASC 606-compliant revenue schedules for SaaS and subscription businesses.
- Synder posts multi-currency transactions with exchange rates set in Xero per line and a separate clearing account for each currency, so you avoid manual FX entries.
- Synder maps items to COGS by their unique accounting product ID, so renaming one doesn’t break the mapping.
- Synder prevents duplicates and imports historical data, and its Smart Rules, which work with Xero in Per Transaction mode, apply custom categorization.

**Where Synder fits:**

- Teams whose order volume is growing into the thousands a month and who want to choose between detailed and summary posting.

**Where Synder falls short:**


- Basic imports run daily rather than hourly.
- Premium integrations such as Faire, Walmart, TikTok, and Clover start at Pro.
- Synder RevRec and free Smart Rules also start at Pro; on Basic and Essential, they are a paid extra.


**Category: Inventory**


### **2. Cin7 Core, best for multi-channel inventory and COGS**

- Product
- Supplier
- Purchase
- Sale


Cin7 Core then pushes the accounting transactions to Xero. Cin7 Core is designed for businesses selling products and/or manufacturing items whose main accounting challenge is in the warehouse rather than the payout.


**Key features**


- Real-time tracking of inventory in several warehouses, along with stock traceability and quantity.
- Purchasing and sales orders management, including light manufacturing (assembly and bill of materials).
- B2B sales site for wholesale purchases.
- Revenue, cost of goods sold, inventory, and stock adjustment reports for Xero, generated from sales and purchasing transactions.


**Pricing** (monthly, excluding taxes, for new customers; annual price not published)

Pro $599/mo 10 users, 4 integrations, 24,000 sale orders/year, MRP


Advanced $1,199/mo 15 users, 6 integrations, 120,000 sale orders/year, advanced warehouse management


**Ideal for:** small to mid-sized product businesses that operate across multiple platforms needing true inventory management feeding accurate cost-of-goods-sold data into Xero.


**Where Cin7 Core fits:**


- Product businesses that sell across several channels and need one stock count for all of them.
- Teams that assemble kits or run light manufacturing alongside resale.

## **Which Xero integrations are worth paying for?**


Pay for a Xero integration when it stops you from handling the same payout, bill, or claim twice.


Free and bundled options cover the basics, and the table below shows when a paid app earns its fee.


### **Free Xero add-ons vs. the best Xero add-ons worth paying for**


**Job** **Free or bundled option** **Paid option** **When the paid option is worth it**


Document capture Hubdoc Dext Prepare You need line-item extraction from multi-line supplier invoices


Shopify sales and payouts Shopify integration by Xero (built with Amaka), free on all Xero plans A payout connector such as Synder You also sell on Amazon or take Stripe or PayPal payments and want every payout reconciled the same way


Bank reconciliation Xero bank feeds and rules A payout reconciliation tool Processor deposits arrive net of fees and refunds and no longer match single sales


**Payback rule:** multiply the hours an app saves each month by the hourly cost of the person doing the work, then compare the result with the subscription. In a hypothetical example, an app that saves 6 hours a month at $50 an hour is worth $300 monthly. That’s more than the entry plan of most paid apps in this guide. As volume grows, payout reconciliation across several channels and sales tax automation for multi-state sellers usually recover their cost first.


## **How to connect apps with Xero: 3 ways to integrate**


You connect an app to Xero in five steps, and most of the configuration happens inside the app itself rather than in Xero. The sequence:


1. Search the[Xero App Store](https://apps.xero.com/us) for the app. Each app detail includes ratings, pricing and the supported Xero plans.
2. Be sure to try the provider since most certified applications have a trial period.
3. Grant access, which will connect the app to your Xero organization via Xero’s secure API.
4. Set up the mapping, determining which accounts sales, fees, refunds and tax post to.
5. Do a preliminary sync and reconcile prior to use at month-end.


Mapping decides whether an integration saves you time, which makes step 4 the one to get right. A robust integration:


- Routes each transaction to the appropriate expense account.
- Maps products to the proper income and COGS accounts.
- Keeps pass-through amounts out of your P&L.


For example, one operator we worked with needed to exclude some customer transactions and apply multiple GL codes to each line of an incoming payout. That level of control is what separates a configurable connector from a rigid one. Map SKUs to Xero items and every fee type to your chart of accounts before the first sync.


Before you configure anything, choose between summary and per-transaction sync, because that choice shapes the rest of the setup.


There are three ways to integrate with Xero, and the right one depends on how much upkeep you can handle:


**Method** **Best for** **Effort** **Who pays Xero’s API costs**

## **Why integration architecture is important for the 2026 close**


Integration architecture matters for the 2026 close because it decides whether your Xero deposits reconcile to payouts or have to be split by hand. One of the biggest monthly manual reconciliation challenges for finance teams is that it’s time consuming, especially as volume increases. The same problems repeat for ecommerce and SaaS companies:


- Payouts arrive in batches with fees already deducted.
- Splitting those batches into a deposit account by hand takes hours.
- Unclassified fees make revenue and margin reporting inaccurate.


That’s why[automating ecommerce bookkeeping](https://synder.com/blog/automate-accounting-processes/) is frequently one of the first enhancements for growing businesses.


The design of the integration is important. Some connectors import orders rather than payouts, but deposits are what should reconcile. The difference comes down to two records:


- Order: what was purchased by the customer
- Payout: what was actually paid after fees, refunds, charge backs, and timing differences


Xero’s newer Shopify integration can sync these, so check which connector and settings you’re using:


- Payouts
- Fees
- Taxes


**Function** **Order-based connector** **Purpose-built payout integration**


What it imports Orders Payouts


Reconciles against the bank? No – order totals don’t match deposits Yes – payout total matches the bank deposit to the cent


Fee separation None – fees stay buried in the net deposit Splits gross revenue, processing fees, refunds, and tax onto separate GL lines


Booking that net deposit as a single sales figure is one of the most common and costly bookkeeping errors. Let’s say, $10,000 in gross sales nets down to a $9,480 bank deposit after **:**


- $370 in processing fees
- $100 in refunds
- $50 in chargebacks


If you code $9,480 to Sales, you’ll:


- Understate revenue by $520
- Hide every fee and refund
- Guarantee your processor statements never match the books


These are four separate line items, and an integration either splits them for you or leaves you to sort them out by hand.


Instead, reconcile payouts through a clearing account, which tracks these separately so you can match them and close the books accurately:


- Fees
- Refunds
- Timing differences


Synder functions like this: the payments appear in a clearing account, while sales and each deduction post on separate lines.


### **Common reconciliation errors and how to fix them**


Most reconciliation failures come down to a few recurring errors, each with a clear fix:


**Common error** **Why it breaks the books** **The fix**


Booking the net deposit as one sales figure Understates revenue, as in the $10,000 example above Split each deposit into separate GL lines at sync


Reconciling against orders, not payouts Order totals never match the bank deposit, so the close won’t tie out Use an integration that reconciles at the payout level


Posting payments straight to the bank Timing and fee differences leave reconciling items that never clear Route every payout through a dedicated clearing account that nets to zero


Recognizing deferred revenue as immediate income Violates ASC 606 by booking unearned cash as earned income Post unearned amounts to a deferred revenue liability, release as earned


Double-counting marketplace facilitator tax Inflates gross revenue or overstates liability, causing wrong state filings Separate facilitator-collected tax from your own native mappings


App bloat and data collision Two apps sync the same orders into Xero, duplicating revenue One source of truth per data type; disable financial sync on the duplicate

## **FAQ**


### **What are the differences between summary sync vs per-transaction sync in Xero?**


Per-transaction sync in Xero posts each order with customer and COGS details for audit-ready records, while summary sync combines transactions into daily or monthly totals that reconcile with the bank statement. Summary sync also makes far fewer calls, which matters under the Xero API rate limit.


### **Is there a way to automate multi-currency payments in Xero without manual FX adjustments?**


You can automate multi-currency payments in Xero without manual FX adjustments when your connector applies the exchange rates set in Xero to every transaction it posts. Check that the tool reads Xero’s rates rather than its own and uses a separate currency clearing account for each denomination. Xero then records any difference between the invoice and payment rates as a realized currency gain or loss, and balances held in Airwallex or Wise can connect to Xero.


### **Can the Xero Established plan integrate with Shopify and Stripe to automate invoicing and cash application for my business?**


The Xero Established plan can integrate with Shopify and Stripe through the Xero App Store, as can the Early and Growing plans. To automate invoicing and cash application, use:


- Stripe to collect invoice payments
- A payout connector to post sales, fees, and deposits


On Early, transactions initiated by app partners may count toward its invoice limit.


### **Which Xero add-ons or integrations do you need for payroll and taxes?**


For payroll and taxes, a US business on Xero needs Gusto or Xero Payroll for wages and Avalara AvaTax for sales tax. Gusto files payroll forms such as IRS Form 941 and W-2s. Avalara adds economic nexus tracking across many states.
